chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is nothing (due) in the wealth of the owned slave, and even if he had a thousand thousand, and even if he was in need, he would not be given anything from the Zakat.
ai.seo_question: Does a slave's personal wealth exempt him from receiving Zakat?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the distinct legal status of a slave's wealth (māl al-ʿabd) in Shia jurisprudence, establishing that while the master owns the slave's assets, the slave retains the personal capacity to pay Zakat on them. It further emphasizes the principle of need-based eligibility, ensuring that even a wealthy slave remains a valid recipient (mustahiqq) of Zakat if he requires financial support, thereby preserving his dignity and autonomy within the household structure.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘There is nothing regarding the wealth of the owned slaves, and even though there may be thousands upon thousand for him, and even if he was in need, he would not be given anything from the Zakāt’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ’Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Zakat is not due on the asset of slaves even if it amounts to a million; but they cannot receive Zakat if they become needy.”’
